principle: Long-form narrative interpretation and memory consolidation are model-owned semantic work. Derived observations remain source-bound, invalidatable and non-authoritative.

narrative.world.purpose: Interpret source-bound long-horizon narrative state without treating derived memory as authority.
rubric: Use only source-bound records visible at the supplied narrative cutoff.
Keep event occurrence time distinct from narration/reveal time.
Track who knows what and when, setup/payoff state, relationship evolution, obligations and causal links when supported by evidence.
Never use future active-plan/review/proposal information as current Canon unless the caller explicitly requests planning context.
Return typed derived observations with source refs; derived observations are not Canon.

reader.expectations.purpose: Interpret which reader-facing questions, promises, setups, relationship expectations, goals or mysteries are currently live and how much pressure they carry.
rubric: Derive expectations only from supplied reader-facing evidence and accepted/locked story history unless planning context is explicitly requested.
Separate an expectation existing in the reader experience from a future planned payoff.
Identify meaningful reinforcement, partial reward, payoff, abandonment or dormancy; do not demand mechanical cliffhangers.
Prefer reader-experience language over author-process language.
Return proposals for ledger updates; the model judgment itself does not mutate Canon.

memory.consolidate.purpose: Propose compact derived memory from bounded accepted/project-provided evidence without replacing source authority.
rubric: Summarize only supplied evidence; preserve uncertainty and source references.
Prefer details likely to matter to current/future story reasoning rather than exhaustive recap.
Do not convert plans, proposals, reviews, research truth or model inference into accepted Canon.
Every derived item must remain invalidatable/rebuildable and cite its sources.
